item.title: Flamingos players shift focus to career development after World Cup success
item.description: Players of Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, say they have shifted focus to personal and career development following their triumph at the 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The players told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in separate interviews that although winning the competition was a major achievement, it marked only the beginning of their football careers. The captain of the team, Chidi Harmony, said the players must put the achievement behind them and concentrate on correcting their mistakes and improving their individual performances. “This is just a starting point. We cannot look at this success and say we have arrived. As young players, we have to put this aside and focus on development. “It is time to work on our mistakes. We want to go out every day and keep improving ourselves so that we can win more trophies for the country,” Harmony said. On her personal ambitions, Harmony said she had identified four or five top European clubs she hoped to play for but declined to disclose their names. “I have four or five big clubs I want to play for, but I will keep them to myself for now. I will share the names the day I finally sign for any of the clubs,” she said. Similarly, Golden Ball winner, Oluebube Umejiaku, expressed gratitude to God for the team’s success in Morocco, saying she was already looking forward to greater achievements. She recalled that following their triumph at the WAFU B tournament in Cote d’Ivoire, the team had resolved to replicate the feat at the World Cup. “After the WAFU B in Cote d’Ivoire, where we won, we told ourselves that we would go and do the same in Morocco, and I am very happy we returned home with the trophy. “Personally, I feel I have not even started. This is just the beginning of my career, and I pray that God helps me achieve more and win more trophies for the country,” Umejiaku said. Forward Kemi Adegbuyi also said she remained determined to achieve greater success, adding that she was focused on improving her game and making further impact in football. She expressed gratitude to God, her family and supporters for their contributions to her success. “I am very happy and grateful to God, my family and those who have been supporting me. “But now, I am focusing on not letting my guard down. I am concentrating on improving myself and making more statements in football,” Adegbuyi said. The FC Robo forward also called for increased investment and support for the Nigerian women’s league to enable more talented players to showcase their abilities. According to her, the league has many undiscovered talents who require adequate platforms and opportunities to develop their careers. “There are a lot of hidden talents in the women’s league in Nigeria. We just need the right platforms to showcase our talents. “We need more investment and support,” she said. (NAN) The post Flamingos players shift focus to career development after World Cup success appeared first on Vanguard News

This matchup won't be a bowl game but it will carry significance: If Texas (7-2, 4-2 SEC) wins, it'll likely need just one more victory this season to seal a spot in the College Football Playoff . If LSU (6-3, 3-3) wins, it'll give its own CFP hopes a boost before a big game against No. 8 Tennessee and a winnable finale against Arkansas. item.title: How Queen's Domain's 2-Person Team Remade Elden Ring's Legacy in a Basement
item.description: At Final Strike Games, Berger met Bradley Boothe, a technical artist and former software engineer who shared a frustration with what could get done at a traditional studio. Together, they struck out on their own, founding the two-person indie studio Freshly Baked Games and trading the security of industry jobs for the creative freedom — and financial uncertainty — of building something entirely theirs. Many years later, the result was a prototype for a game… that was way too ambitious (but they fully intend to return to). So they went back to a different concept, a stripped-down first-person fantasy inspired by FromSoftware's cult-classic King's Field . That was supposed to take a year to build. Three years later, the game, Queen’s Domain , is an ambitious torrent of weaponry, monster encounters, and Berger’s patented 3D level design, all spread across an low-poly open-world map.

item.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
item.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them. How and when I'm watching it Counting the stars you can see in the Pleiades is a fun way to test your naked-eye observing skills. item.title: CM Punk’s WWE Retirement May Be Near Following HUGE Rumor About New Backstage Role
item.description: WWE CM Punk’s time as an active WWE wrestler may be closer to an end than fans thought after a big rumor about a new backstage role inside the company. There were many who doubted Punk was capable of having a successful second run in WWE. He left over a decade ago on really bad terms, then when he returned to the industry with AEW five years ago — after many years away from it — that relationship also ended poorly. Including a couple of backstage fights. However, three years after his shocking return at Survivor Series 2023, all reports since suggest the WWE legend is a beloved member of the roster. He is willing to do whatever it takes to promote the brand and impart his wisdom on younger stars. It has created an unexpected bond between him and the company’s head of creative, Triple H, after the two butted heads years ago. Well, it seems that the trust and admiration that WWE decision-makers have for CM Punk is so strong that he is allegedly being eyed for a major backstage role. According to PW Insider, Punk is in the early stages of training to be Shawn Michaels’ replacement in NXT. The outlet reported last month that Michaels is expected to replace retiring WWE executive Bruce Pritchard next year. In Friday’s story, they noted that the Hall of Famer will soon start “splitting his time between NXT and WWE HQ to prepare for that transition.” It is why they claim “Punk has been at the majority of WWE NXT broadcasts in recent weeks alongside Michaels and is currently being prepped for that role.” CM Punk is an inspired choice to take over NXT The PW Insider report notes that there is no clear timeline on when Punk would bring his in-ring career to a close since “the company wants everyone involved to take time to ensure it’s the right fit for all involved.” Nevertheless, they want him to be the man to guide NXT into the future. Most assumed the 48-year-old would try to compete into his 50s. Especially since he is currently in the best shape of his career and doesn’t have the same mileage as most stars his age because he was away from the business for a decade. The idea of him retiring soon will surely disappoint many WWE fans since several other greats have ended their careers over the last few years. However, of the potential options to lead NXT, Punk is a fascinating choice. Obviously, he does not have experience running a promotion and TV show. But neither did Michaels, and he has done a very good job in the role. Besides that, the future Hall of Famer has done a lot in the wrestling industry and can offer a ton of valuable advice to prospects. Punk rose from the independent scene to become a top star in WWE despite not having a classic “look.” He has always been a talented mat wrestler, but he is a master at storytelling in the ring. Yet, he is probably best known for his skills on the mic and how valuable that ability is in becoming a star. item.title: UTSA, basketball coach Austin Claunch part ways following DWI arrest
item.description: UTSA men's basketball coach Austin Claunch, center, watches his team during practice at the new Basketball & Volleyball Training Center in San Antonio on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) UTSA and men's basketball coach Austin Claunch have mutually agreed to part ways, Roadrunners athletics director Lisa Campos announced Friday, ending his tenure after two seasons in the wake of an arrest on suspicion of DWI . Acting head coach Nick Bowman, a longtime Claunch assistant, will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season after leading the Roadrunners to a 2-1 start. Austin Claunch, 36, is pictured in a mugshot at the Nueces County jail. He is charged with driving while intoxicated. (Courtesy of the Corpus Christi Police Department) "After thoughtful discussions about the future of the program, we mutually agreed that this was the right time for a transition," Campos said in a statement. "We thank Coach Claunch for his efforts over the last two years and wish him nothing but the best in the future. We look forward to this season with Nick Bowman at the helm." Less than a week before the start of the season, Claunch was found passed out behind the wheel of his Mercedes-Benz 350 Series at 2 a.m. on Oct. 27 in a Stripes parking lot in Corpus Christi, per the arrest report. The report from the Corpus Christi police department states that officers found Claunch unconscious, wearing his seatbelt with the vehicle running and the door left open. The initial call to law enforcement said Claunch had been "stumbling around" the store, and he responded with thick, slurred speech when the officers woke him. He admitted that he had been drinking and drove himself to the Stripes store, and he performed poorly on the field sobriety tests , per the arrest report. He refused blood and breath tests, and he was transported to an area hospital. His suspension was announced the next day, and the Roadrunners opened the season under Bowman's leadership on Nov. 2. "I want to thank our players, staff, administration, and fans for the support they've shown me during my time at UTSA," Claunch said in a statement Friday. "Dr. Campos and I agreed that it was best for both sides to move in a different direction. I want to thank Dr. Campos for the opportunity to coach at UTSA. I'll always be rooting for UTSA and the young men in this program." Because Claunch and UTSA mutually agreed to part ways, neither side is owed a buyout or any financial compensation, per a UTSA spokesperson. Claunch was hired in April 2024 on a five-year contract that ran through the 2028-29 season at an annual guaranteed compensation $550,000, and Claunch would have been owed 65% of his remaining guaranteed compensation if UTSA fired him without cause. Bowman came to UTSA as an assistant on Claunch's initial staff in April 2024 following a year as the lead assistant and recruiting coordinator at New Orleans. item.title: Steeler who had Week 3 Burrow strip sack won't face Bengals | Report
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Derrick Harmon isn't expected to return from a foot injury to face the Cincinnati Bengals ahead of their NFL Week 10 showdown on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium, according to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Ray Fittipaldo . Harmon hasn't played since suffering a foot injury Oct. 1 against Cleveland. Harmon was considered the Steelers' biggest question mark for Week 10 on the team's injury report . He was designated to return from injured reserve and practiced Thursday and Friday, but was limited. "We'll see by tomorrow," Harmon told reporters after Friday's practice. With 53 seconds left in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers in Pittsburgh in Week 3, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow fumbled as he was sacked by Harmon at the Pittsburgh 46-yard line. The ball was recovered by Pittsburgh's Sebastian Joseph-Day at the Cincinnati 49. Harmon beat Bengals offensive lineman Dalton Risner to get to Burrow. "We've got to be better," Burrow said after the game. "… You can't shoot yourself in the foot . Can't win in this league like that." Bengals tight ends Erick All Jr. and Tanner Hudson were adamant after the game that All recovered Burrow's fumble. All said a Pittsburgh player was just laying on the ball, but it was All who secured it. The call didn't go the Bengals' way. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Steeler who had Week 3 Burrow strip sack won't face Bengals | Report

item.title: Wright Motorsports Bets On Sargent For Full-Time 2027 IMSA Title Run
item.description: The GTD Wright Motorsports Porsche 911 of Adam Adelson, Callum Ilott and Tom Sargent (120) drives off Turn 12 in the IMSA Motul SportsCar Endurance Grand Prix on Sunday, August 2, 2026, at Road America in Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tom Sargent is no longer just a substitute driver for Wright Motorsports. He gets the wheel for the full 2027 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship season. The 25-year-old Australian replaces Callum Ilott to partner with team owner Adam Adelson in the #120 Porsche 911 GT3 R. This shift marks a clear move toward stability and chemistry over a fresh roster. DailySportsCar confirmed the promotion on November 11, 2026, ending two years of Sargent as an endurance-only specialist. Wright Motorsports has seen enough of Sargent to trust him with a full season. Following his contribution to podium finishes at Sebring and Watkins Glen in 2026, the team recognizes his worth. These results show he can handle the pressure of the biggest races. The team now wants that consistency across every single round of the championship. A Calculated Move for the Title The decision to keep the core together makes sense for a team chasing a crown. Adelson and Sargent have already shown they work well together on the track. A difficult opening at Daytona preceded their seventh-place result in the GTD standings last year. Watkins Glen saw a second-place finish while Sebring yielded third place as they rebounded. This bounce-back proves the pairing can handle adversity. Adelson sees this as a natural next step for a driver he has watched grow. “The growth of Wright Motorsports over the past few seasons has been incredibly rewarding, and I am excited about what lies ahead for us in 2027,” said Adelson. He added that having Sargent for the full season is something he is particularly looking forward to. Sargent is ready to take the leap from part-time to full-time. He spent his first two years learning the series and the car. Now he has the experience to compete for wins every weekend. “I will be returning for my third year now with Wright Motorsports, but this time as their full-time IMSA driver. To say I’m excited is an understatement,” said Sargent. He noted that both he and Adelson have improved a lot. The pair aims to build on their past accomplishments and fight for the championship. This is not a gamble on a rookie. It is a promotion of a driver who has already earned his spot. Why the Full-Time Role Matters Now Full-time drives in IMSA are rare and hard to get. Most drivers jump between teams or sit out endurance rounds. Sargent staying with one team for the whole season gives Wright Motorsports a major edge. Continuity allows for better setup work and race strategy. The team has won five IMSA races and holds championships in multiple series. They need a driver who can deliver those results week in and week out. Sargent has the talent to do just that. He won the first and last races of 2026 and finished ru

item.title: Germany U21 1-2 Belgium U21: Di Salvo's depleted side suffer first defeat of 2026
item.description: Germany U21 1-2 Belgium U21: Di Salvo's depleted side suffer first defeat of 2026 Due to players getting nominated for the senior side by Jürgen Klopp and many injuries, Germany looked very different from the side that played the majority of the qualification campaign for the European championship. However, they had the first two chances with Anton Kade's blocked effort and Paris Brunner's off-target shot. The next five minutes belonged to Belgium as Julian Duranville scored with his second attempt of the game. A minute after his solo effort narrowly missed the target, the former BVB winger had the simplest task of converting a tap-in after Lucas Stassin's cutback. Germany regained control after conceding the opening goal, with Muhammed Damar playing a big part in most of their promising attacks. The Wolfsburg midfielder was also the one who brought the hosts back in Essen twenty minutes before the half-time break. Lucas Noubi's challenge on Brunner gave Germany a free-kick opportunity from close range, which was calmly converted by Damar. The Hoffenheim loanee scored with the brilliant tactic of hitting it under the wall. The 22-year-old last played for Antonio Di Salvo's side a year ago, but he played a starring role in the absence of star names. Belgium's goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans saved his next attempt after a deflection as Damar decided to go alone in a 4 vs. 3 counter-attacking situation. Stassin hit the post with the last meaningful action of the first-half, although Germany were on top for the most part. It was Germany's turn to be denied by three woodwork early after the restart as the “Man of the Hour” Damar hit the crossbar moments before Kade's header narrowly missed the target. Damar and Kade created several promising opportunities in the final third, but they were among the first players to be taken off by Di Salvo. However, it was Belgium's substitute Romeo Vermant who scored within seconds of entering the game. Nicolo Tresoldi's Club Brugge teammate nutmegged Dennis Seimen to put the visitors ahead for the second time in the game. Brunner hit the sidenetting from a promising position before Brughmans made some decent saves to deny substitutes Maurice Krattenmacher and Merit Kömür. Debutant Louey Ben Farhat also came close to leveling the score for the hosts with his first action of the game. Nonetheless, Belgium U21 held on to their slender lead to beat their Germany counterparts for the third time in a row. After eight successive wins in the Euros qualifying campaign, Di Salvo's suffered their first defeat in 2026. Germany U21 will end the year with a friendly against Croatia in Rijeka on Tuesday.

item.title: Tinubu flags off $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport construction
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Friday flagged off the construction of the 3.5 billion dollar Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River. Tinubu, represented by the vice-president, Kashim Shettima, described the project as a historic economic intervention capable of transforming Nigeria’s maritime industry. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony in Bakassi, Tinubu said the project would break a centuries-old jinx and reposition Cross River as a major commercial and maritime hub. “I have not come to Calabar to cut a ribbon and dance Ekpe Masquerade. I am here to break ground and break centuries-old jinx,” he said. He said the project would unlock Nigeria’s maritime potential, diversify the economy and demonstrate what collective commitment could achieve. The President said the seaport, supported by a proposed superhighway, would provide an evacuation corridor linking the South-South to other parts of the country. He said the concentration of more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade through Lagos ports had contributed to congestion, shipment delays and higher costs. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in faith. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its load on one shoulder. “When over 80 per cent of our foreign trade flows through Lagos, and Lagos alone, that is not strength. That is congestion,” he said. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would complement existing ports, improve cargo movement and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in international trade. He said Nigeria accounted for more than 60 per cent of West Africa’s Gross Domestic Product but handled only 25 per cent of regional cargo traffic. The president said the country’s blue economy had the potential to generate 44 billion dollars annually. “The sea is no longer just water to look at. It is wealth to harvest,” he said. He said the project would create employment opportunities for engineers, crane operators, truck drivers, welders, customs officers, artisans and traders. Tinubu added that agricultural produce, including cocoa from Ikom and rice from Ogoja, alongside timber and solid minerals, would benefit from improved access to international markets. He urged Cross River residents to protect the project from political interference and misinformation. Earlier, Gov. Bassey Otu described the groundbreaking as a milestone in efforts to reposition Cross River as a major player in Nigeria’s maritime and blue economy. Otu said the project, initiated under his predecessor, Prof. Ben Ayade, had suffered political, administrative, legal and environmental setbacks. He thanked Tinubu for supporting the project and providing the necessary federal government approvals. The governor said the state had completed environmental impact assessments, hydrographic, geotechnical and geophysical surveys. He added that the project had secured technical approval from the Federal Executive Council. Otu said the seaport would be developed through a public-private partnership arrangemen

item.title: RB Leipzig join race for one of 2008's most valuable defenders
item.description: RB Leipzig join race for one of 2008's most valuable defenders RB Leipzig are already looking towards the summer transfer window, with an exciting defensive prospect reportedly on their radar. According to Sky , the Bundesliga side have identified Udinese youngster Matteo Palma as a potential addition to their backline. The 18-year-old Berlin-born centre-back has quickly made a name for himself in Italy, earning regular first-team minutes this season. Palma has made seven competitive appearances for Udinese, scoring once, and currently boasts a market value of €8 million (according to Transfermarkt). That makes him one of the most valuable centre-backs in the world born in 2008. Interestingly, Palma is no stranger to German football. The defender came through Hertha BSC's academy before moving to Udinese in 2022. He also represented Germany at U16 and U17 level before opting to play for Italy internationally just recently. Leipzig could certainly use some “fresh blood” at the back. Castello Lukeba is attracting interest from several European heavyweights, while veteran Willi Orban's contract is approaching its expiry. Palma is reportedly one of several names on the shortlist as the Bundesliga club prepare for a potential defensive overhaul.

item.title: WWE legend John Cena addresses wardrobe controversy with fiery NSFW response

Speaking to Sports Illustrated, he responded to the controversy . He clarified that he wasn’t wearing jean shorts, or jorts, but rather cargo shorts. “Those weren’t jorts in Brooklyn, and they weren’t jorts on NXT. I’m wearing cargo shorts,” Cena adamantly said. “I’m not wearing any wristbands, I don’t have a towel, and I don’t have any knee pads. So, when I said the jorts are retired, the f**king jorts are retired.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He also explained that he wore an outfit that was closer to his gear from his days as an in-ring competitor because he feels “most at home” in them. He wanted to run to the ring and run the ropes. item.title: Aston Martin F1 Problems Persist; Honda Under Pressure
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Three races remain in the 2026 Formula 1 season, and for Aston Martin, the end of this disappointing season can’t come quickly enough. It has been a rough year for the Silverstone-based team, which had high hopes of competing amid the new regulations and the addition of legendary designer Adrian Newey, who took over as team principal. Unfortunately for Aston Martin and the Stroll family, it has been the team’s worst season since returning to the grid in 2021, with only seven points through 20 races. Aston Martin ranks 10th in the Constructors’ Championship, only ahead of Cadillac, which joined the Formula 1 grid as a brand new entrant this year. For many teams, upgrades and developments throughout a season address problems, but throughout the grand prix schedule, they have continued to be plagued with issues and have very few positives to take from the year. Aston Martin’s PU Problems Persist The problems started almost immediately, with the AMR26 suffering severe vibrations that forced Fernando Alonso to retire on Lap 21 of the Australian Grand Prix. Lance Stroll’s car had similar issues, and he eventually finished 15 laps down after limping around for data-gathering purposes. With Newey able to work on improving the aerodynamic side of the car, which ultimately led to a B-spec being introduced at the Hungarian Grand Prix, the main issue has primarily been reliability and power issues with the team’s Honda power unit. The team has struggled for pace all year, regularly finishing towards the back of the grid, and Stroll made recent comments on how much Aston Martin was losing compared to the rest of the field. “We’re really struggling on the engine side. We know that, so a lot of work to be done,” he told reporters before the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. “We’re missing two seconds [a lap] in engines, so it’s difficult.” With Alonso finishing qualifying in Malaysia two seconds behind pole sitter Max Verstappen, Stroll’s comments suggest that there is a lot more the car could offer if Honda’s power unit was on par with its competitors, such as Mercedes, Ferrari, and even Red Bull Powertrains. Throughout the year, Aston Martin have also struggled to see out races largely due to reliability issues, which have seen Alonso retire from seven races and Stroll retire from 13. Such issues have limited what either driver could do, with Alonso claiming all of the team’s points with a season-high P8 coming in Malaysia. Stroll, meanwhile, has had the worst of it and also achieved his best performance in Malaysia with a P12 finish, with just six race finishes. Stroll has had such a difficult year that he is one retirement away from tying the Formula 1 record for most DNFs in a season, which is currently held by two drivers: Andrea de Cesaris (Minardi 1986, Brabham 1987) and Rubens Barrichello (Stewart 1997). item.title: Estonia latest country to ban Russian athletes
item.description: Estonia shares a border with Russia [Getty Images] Estonia has become the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine. It comes after Norway, Finland and Canada made similar announcements. The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus. In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality". They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military. Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms. However, it has now emerged that Estonia's government has written to the FIS, claiming that allowing entry to competitors from Russia and Belarus would undermine the country's support of Ukraine, and present an opportunity for propaganda. In a statement issued to BBC Sport, the FIS said it "is committed to offering full support to athletes, national ski associations and local organisers - with most of which we have a long-standing relationship - in the process of navigating what we know to be a very complex situation. "With that said, the Individual Neutral Athlete policy is clear in stating that notwithstanding eligibility, the host country visa and entry policies remain in place and are determined solely by the host country. FIS bears no responsibility for denial of visas or entry to any person granted eligibility under the FIS Individual Neutral Athlete Policy." On Thursday, Scandinavian neighbours Norway and Finland both said they would also block visas for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine. Norway is preparing to host the cross-country skiing World Cup next month, while Finland is due to stage the figure skating world championships in March. The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland. This comes in the wake of last month's decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to overturn a ban of Russia by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), a move condemned by the British, German, Finnish and Czech federations. Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022, but the Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) then successfully appealed that decision at Cas. The court said that IIHF arguments citing safety and security were "not supported by sufficient evidence", but the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said the ruling caused "special outrage". item.title: Mauricio Pochettino set for USMNT send-offs before Manchester United gig
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino set for USMNT send-offs before Manchester United gig By Charles Boehm It’s been in the works all week, then Mauricio Pochettino and U.S. Soccer made it official on Friday morning. The US men’s national team ’s upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal series vs. Haiti will be the Argentine’s swan song as head coach, before he and his core staff depart to take the helm at beleaguered English Premier League giants Manchester United. "I want to say thank you, thank you, thank you so much," Pochettino said during his matchday-1 press conference ahead of Saturday’s first-leg clash at Inter Miami CF ’s Nu Stadium, which Haiti have selected as their home venue due to chronic instability in their homeland (4:30 pm ET). "The last two years, I think you made me feel really well, really happy doing my job, sharing an amazing project, being part of this family. It is difficult now for me to talk because I am a very emotional guy. "We learn a lot from you all, from this country, those amazing people. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions in our career." Emotional farewell ‘Poch’ and his assistants renewed their contracts with U.S. Soccer just a few months ago, signing through the 2030 FIFA World Cup shortly after this year’s tournament run ended with a 4-1 loss to Belgium in the Round of 16. His work in the September/October camp also reflected a long-term mindset, with Cavan Sullivan , Julian Hall and six other teenagers among the host of newcomers handed their debut caps with the USMNT in four impressive friendly victories. "What you've done with the men's and the boys program in two years has been unbelievable," said federation president Cindy Parlow Cone. "Not only have you contributed to their advancement. You've contributed to the entire federation being better, and you have been such a great partner to all of us. "We obviously are in a stronger place today than we were two years ago," Parlow Cone added. "We have great veteran leadership with a mix of young players that are up and coming, as we've seen through the last window, and then hopefully they'll show it during this window as well. We have a great foundation and lots to build upon, and I am energized about our future." Storied club Yet when one of the world’s most iconic clubs comes calling, it’s hard for anyone to resist. Let alone a manager with Pochettino’s experience, admiration and distinct sense of unfinished business in the Premier League, where he became a global name during a sterling stint in charge of Tottenham Hotspur from 2014-19. "It's not too many opportunities that can happen in your career like a side [like] Manchester United, and of course, when that arrives, it's difficult to turn down that situation," he admitted. "But what I want to make clear, when we decide together to extend our commitment, always was the commitment for the federation. "We recover our motivation," he added about his reinvigorating adventure in North America. "We recover

item.title: How Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reacted to CFP expansion
item.description: LAWRENCE — Kansas football coach Lance Leipold shared his support for the expansion of the College Football Playoff this past Monday, Nov. 9, following the announcement that the postseason event would be moving to 24 teams with the 2027-28 season. Leipold, whose time in coaching includes competing in playoffs at Division III-level Wisconsin-Whitewater previously in his career, understands there are a lot of components to consider at the Division I level. That includes what’s going to happen with bowl games. But he thinks this can be a good thing for the sport, which currently has a 12-team playoff. Leipold pointed to the NFL and how it’s nowhere near as big a deal if the top team loses a regular-season game there as it is in college. From his perspective, college has to get used to the idea that teams will compete in the playoffs in the future with more losses than they’ve had in the past. It’s the new normal. RELATED: Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reflects on key play from UCF loss “All in all, I think it’s good for opportunities,” Leipold told reporters. “I think it’s great. I think we have to continue to manage the calendar as good as we can, for the sake of the game. But, yeah, I think it’s where it was going and as soon as it went to four, I knew it’d keep going. And will it get to 32? We shall see.” Leipold noted he didn’t think it’d be something that would diminish the regular season, as some have debated, as long as at least two rounds can be played on home fields and there isn’t too much of a turn toward neutral sites. The ability to have some level of home-field advantage as something to play for during the regular season is something he considers to be significant for any team and fan base. Also, the more the playoff expands, the more demand there is on programs and fans to travel and use more financial resources. The 24-team edition of the College Football Playoff is set to have 16 of its 23 games played on campus, with those matchups taking place during the first two rounds. The quarterfinals and semifinals will continue to be played at the College Football Playoff’s bowl partner locations. The first championship game of the 24-team format will be played in New Orleans in 2028. Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. He was the 2022 National Sports Media Association’s sportswriter of the year for the state of Kansas. Contact him at JMGuskey@usatodayco.com or on Twitter at @JordanGuskey. item.title: Manchester United confirm new head coach ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: Manchester United confirm new head coach ahead of Liverpool clash Mauricio Pochettino Faces Liverpool Test as Manchester United Reset Begins Manchester United have done what desperate clubs do when results collapse and the table starts to look ugly. They have changed the manager. Mauricio Pochettino is in, Michael Carrick is out, and his first proper problem arrives immediately, Liverpool at Anfield. There is no gentle introduction here. United are 18th, they have eight points from 10 league games, and the numbers under Carrick were heading in one direction. His last game summed it up, a chaotic 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa in which United needed two stoppage-time goals just to scrape a point. Entertaining, maybe. Sustainable, clearly not. Pochettino appointment made at speed United confirmed Pochettino on Friday, one day after Carrick was dismissed. He has signed a deal running until the summer of 2029, with the club reportedly paying around £7.4 million to release him from his contract with the United States national team. The pitch from United is familiar enough. High-intensity football, attacking ideas, young players improving. All well and good, but right now this is about stabilising a side that has won only three of 15 matches in all competitions this season, with just one league victory. Pochettino returns to English football after spells at Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea. His CV in England remains respectable rather than glittering. He reached the League Cup and Champions League finals with Tottenham, but did not win either. At Paris Saint-Germain, he did at least collect Ligue 1 and the French Cup. Anfield comes too soon for comfort Timing matters, and for United this timing is awkward. Pochettino will first oversee the United States in Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on November 14 and 17. He then begins officially at Old Trafford on Wednesday, meets the squad, runs training on Thursday and has three days to prepare for Liverpool on Sunday, November 22. That is barely enough time to learn names, never mind install a system. He will have to rely on clarity and simplicity. Organise the team, tighten the distances, stop the chaos. Anything more sophisticated can wait. Carrick exit reflects deeper problems Carrick’s dismissal ends a brief reign that never gained traction. He had taken over in January after Ruben Amorim’s departure and earned a full-time deal after securing Champions League qualification. Since then, the drop has been severe. Fifteen matches into a two-year contract signed in May, he is gone. The only league win came in a 5-2 result against Ipswich on August 30. Everything else left United drifting towards the bottom three. That is why Pochettino has been hired. Not for sentiment, not for long-term theory, but because United need points, structure and credibility, starting at Anfield.

item.title: Arokodare double secures Nigeria win in Afcon 2027 qualifier
item.description: Tolu Arokodare has scored 13 goals in 17 appearances this season after joining Ajax on loan from Wolves [Getty Images] Tolu Arokodare was the hero as Nigeria boosted their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) with a 3-1 home win over tournament co-hosts Tanzania. With the East Africans already assured of a spot at the finals, the Super Eagles are battling for the one qualification spot available in Group L and have little margin for error after losing 3-0 in Guinea-Bissau in September. Alhassan Yusuf kept his composure to slot Nigeria into a second-minute lead in Uyo from Ademola Lookman's pass, but the visitors equalised through Alphonce Msanga just after the half-hour mark. Arokodare climbed off the bench at half-time and cleverly flicked home Wilfred Ndidi's low ball to restore the lead for the West Africans in the 52nd minute. And the Ajax striker, who is on a season-long loan from Wolves, gave the Super Eagles breathing space eight minutes later when he controlled Moses Usor's cross from the left and smashed in from 12 yards out. With three games played in the group, Eric Chelle's side are now one point behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who drew 1-1 with Madagascar on Thursday. Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss Elsewhere, Tunisia are in danger of missing out on the finals for the first time since 1992 after suffering a 2-0 defeat at home against Libya, and Kenya scored a last-minute equaliser to end South Africa's perfect start. Later on Friday Ali Maher takes charge of Egypt for the first time following the departure of Hossam Hassan when the Pharaohs host Malawi (19:00 GMT). Meanwhile, Morocco look to extend their perfect start in Group A with a home game against Niger (20:00 GMT). The third round of qualifying culminates with three games on Saturday, while the fourth round of fixtures are split across Monday and Tuesday. Tunisia downed as McCarthy frustrates Bafana Former South Africa international Benni McCarthy denied Bafana Bafana victory as his Kenya side grabbed a late equaliser [Reuters] Tunisia have appeared at a record 17 consecutive Afcons but are winless and bottom of Group H - another section with just one qualifying place on offer - after defeat by their North African neighbours Libya. The Carthage Eagles could complain about refereeing decisions going against them in Sfax, with Ali Maaloul penalised for a shirt pull on Muad Eisay just before half-time and Ali Youssef converting the resulting spot-kick. Tunisia had a goal ruled out following a marginal offside call in the second half and three minutes later a low shot from Hamdou El Houni made it 2-0 to the Mediterranean Knights. Libya, who last played at an Afcon in 2012, climb to second in the table and go level on points with Uganda. South Africa are a point clear of Guinea at the top of Group D after a 2-2 draw against Benni McCarthy's Kenya in Johannesburg. item.title: One single matchup that gives Michigan some hope against Oregon
item.description: Not much has gone right for Michigan this college football season. So little that head coach Kyle Whittingham could suddenly find himself on the chopping block when all is said and done after just one year. Heading into a road test against resurgent Oregon, the Wolverines could be headed for yet more disaster. But one matchup on the field might give them a fighting chance. Strength vs. strength Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola celebrates a touchdown by Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans on Sept. 26, 2026, at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Oregon enters its Saturday showdown as a 10.5-point favorite, but Michigan has one significant matchup advantage that could make this considerably more competitive: its elite pass defense against Oregon’s passing attack. The Wolverines are allowing just 154.8 passing yards per game, ranking fourth nationally. They have also surrendered only eight passing touchdowns this season. For an Oregon offense averaging 285.4 passing yards per game, sitting top 15 in FBS, that represents a credible challenge. Pressure without blitzing Michigan’s defensive front makes this matchup particularly dangerous. The Wolverines have recorded 21 sacks and 53 tackles for loss, demonstrating their ability to disrupt quarterbacks before routes develop. Defensive lineman John Henry Daley leads the team with six sacks and nine tackles for loss. If he consistently wins his individual battles against Oregon’s blockers, quarterback Dylan Raiola could face uncomfortable decisions and hurried throws. That matters because Raiola has thrown for 1,354 yards, 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Protecting that efficiency against Michigan’s pressure will be essential. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 11’s biggest games Numbers favor Michigan’s defense The contrast is striking. Oregon is a potent aerial offense, while Michigan ranks fourth nationally in total defense, surrendering only 255.3 yards per game on average. Michigan also has veteran defensive backs capable of challenging Oregon’s receivers in man coverage. Will that be enough? Almost certainly not, considering Michigan basically can’t move the ball. But the Wolverines’ pass rush and secondary present a legitimate opportunity early on. That could theoretically slow down the Ducks’ aerial attack enough to make it close. If the Wolverines consistently pressure Raiola and eliminate explosive passing plays, they could make Oregon’s comfortable betting favorite status look a little more questionable. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Tiger Woods remembers Dan Hicks after unexpected death: ‘A great friend to me’
item.description: Tiger Woods paid tribute to late NBC Sports golf voice Dan Hicks , calling the longtime broadcaster "a great friend to me both on and off the course" following Hicks' unexpected death at 64. "Dan Hicks was beloved by all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him," Woods said in a statement mourning Hicks, who died Nov. 11 as a result of an acute illness. "His kindness, warmth, and presence will be deeply missed. Like so many in the golf world, Dan was a great friend to me both on and off the course. I had the utmost respect for him and the incredible job he did for our sport for decades." For more than a quarter-century, Hicks was the defining soundtrack to Woods' career, calling 27 of his PGA Tour victories — including Woods' iconic 12-foot birdie putt on the 72nd hole at Torrey Pines to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open , punctuated by Hicks' timeless call: "Expect anything different?" "Our thoughts are with Hannah and their daughters during this incredibly difficult time," Woods added, referring to Hicks' wife, fellow broadcaster Hannah Storm, and their three daughters, Hannah, Ellery, and Riley. "I hope they find comfort in knowing how much he meant to so many people and the lasting impact he made on everyone whose life he touched." View this post on Instagram Storm announced her husband's passing on social media , remembering him as "truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around." Born and raised in Tucson, Arizona, Hicks graduated from Sabino High School and the University of Arizona before starting in local radio and television. After joining CNN in 1989 and moving to NBC Sports in 1992, he worked as a tower announcer until being named lead golf play-by-play voice in 2000. Beyond anchoring NBC's coverage of the U.S. Open, The Open Championship , Ryder Cup, Presidents Cup and FedEx Cup Playoffs, Hicks was a versatile fixture across sports — calling Olympic swimming and skiing, including the U.S. men's freestyle relay comeback at the 2008 Beijing Games, and returning as the lead voice for Notre Dame Football in 2024. Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: Tiger Woods remembers Dan Hicks after unexpected death: ‘A great friend to me’

item.title: Vanderbilt’s Offense Collapses To 103rd In SEC Scoring
item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images SEC Week 11 matchups favor teams with strong defenses and clean ball handling. Vanderbilt sits at 103rd in scoring with just 23 points per game, a massive drop from their top-8 rank last year. Oklahoma needs to force mistakes to beat a dangerous Ole Miss offense. The Sooners must protect quarterback John Mateer and stop Trinidad Chambliss from running wild. Yahoo Sports reports that the Commodores have lost their spark since the Diego Pavia era ended. Tim Beck returns as offensive coordinator, but his power-spread scheme faces a new reality. The team relies heavily on receiver Junior Sherrill, who has 56 catches for 747 yards. No other player on the roster has more than 17 catches. This one-dimensional attack makes it easy for opponents to stack the box. Vanderbilt’s Quarterback Struggles Jared Curtis was the number two overall recruit last year and chose Vandy over Georgia. He has a big arm and runs well, but he looks like a true freshman in the SEC. Curtis averages over 11 yards per completion, yet he has thrown eight interceptions on only 224 attempts. Yahoo Sports notes that the offense lacks depth beyond Sherrill and running back Sedrick Alexander. Alexander used to gain more than five yards per carry, but now he sits at 333 yards with a 3.9 average. His change-of-pace partner, Makhilyn Young, cannot break off big runs either. The quarterback run game puts too much pressure on Curtis, who is not ready for this level yet. The offensive line changes have held the team back all season. Without a balanced attack, Alabama and other top teams will dominate these matchups. Oklahoma’s Path to Victory Oklahoma faces a tough test against Ole Miss this Saturday. To secure victory, the Sooners must execute perfectly on offense and defense alike. John Mateer must play smart and avoid turnovers. One mistake gives the Rebels short fields and extra possessions. Mateer requires the offensive line to shield him and provide ample time within the pocket. Running the ball effectively is key to opening up the passing game. The defense must find a way to contain Trinidad Chambliss. In Ole Miss’ 34-26 win a year ago, he passed for 315 yards against the Sooners. That single stat shows the challenge he presents. An injury sidelines Kewan Lacy for this game, potentially affecting the Rebels’ running game. However, the offense remains dangerous when it gets rolling. The defensive front must maintain pass-rush lanes and collapse the pocket. Third-down defense is another critical area for Oklahoma. The team ranks in the top five nationally in defensive third-down efficiency. This strength needs to continue against a good offensive team. Ole Miss has struggled in this area lately, but they can still score if given enough opportunities. The defense must get off the field and give the ball back to the offense. item.title: Yankees rumors: New York linked to ex-Padres star reliever in free agency
item.description: Credit: David Frerker-Imagn Images Yankees rumors: New York linked to ex-Padres star reliever in free agency appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With rumors surrounding the New York Yankees this offseason regarding who the team will target in free agency, the latest reporting suggests that pitching will be a need to address. As the Yankees look to bolster their team through free agency , this MLB insider has linked the team to a top relief pitcher on the market. According to Jorge Castillo of ESPN, New York is “interested in signing” reliever Adrian Morejon, who has played with the San Diego Padres since 2019 and is now a free agent. Last season, Morejon recorded a 2.83 ERA with 107 strikeouts, a 1.08 WHIP, and a career-high 28 holds in 86 innings, but Castillo noted that they would pursue the reliever if David Bednar “ends up elsewhere,” though the waiting game could impact everything. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The Yankees are interested in signing left-hander Adrian Morejon — the best free agent reliever — if Bednar ends up elsewhere,” Castillo continued. “Waiting for Bednar’s decision, however, could hamper that pursuit. General manager Brian Cashman has avoided giving relievers big contracts in recent years, but he said this week that he’s ‘not afraid to do it’ should the opportunity surface.” More on the Yankees’ situation with David Bednar Looking at the Yankees’ situation with Bednar, the closer last season recorded a 2.47 ERA to go along with 76 strikeouts, a 1.04 WHIP, and 35 saves. Castillo says that New York is “waiting to see” if the veteran will sign the one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer, as he has until Tuesday to do it, though a multiyear contract is still in question. “Bednar, 32, would undoubtedly garner a multiyear deal — with the Yankees or another club — if he declines the contract. But he could take it and hit free agency next winter without the weight of draft compensation hindering his market,” Castillo wrote. At any rate, it remains to be seen if Bednar resigns with the Yankees or if the team loses him and the ball club gets Morejon, as the team looks to further improve after finishing with a 93-68 record, putting them second in the AL East. New York would be swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. item.title: Spurs fans can watch Warriors showdown for free on CW 35. Here's how
item.description: Spurs vs. Warriors airs free on CW 35 tonight. Here's how to watch on DAZN, Prime Video or local TV, plus upcoming free Spurs games. (Nam Y. Huh/Associated Press) San Antonio Spurs fans won't have to shell out for another streaming subscription to watch Friday's game against the Golden State Warriors. The Spurs return to Frost Bank Center to face Golden State, with the game airing on DAZN and Prime Video. San Antonio-area fans can also watch for free on CW 35. The game tips off at 8:30 p.m. San Antonio enters on a 10-game winning streak after sweeping a four-game road trip through Sacramento, Portland, Phoenix and Chicago. Fans hoping to see Victor Wembanyama face Stephen Curry will have to wait. Curry is out after an MRI confirmed an oblique abdominal tear, according to the Warriors. Despite Curry's absence, the matchup gives San Antonio another chance to build on its early-season momentum against a familiar Western Conference rival. ALSO READ: Spurs add De'Aaron Fox to injury list ahead of NBA Cup game against Warriors How to watch Spurs vs. Warriors Fans in the San Antonio area can watch Friday's game through several options: • CW SA (CW 35): Free over-the-air broadcast on channel 4.2 with a compatible antenna. Cable and satellite availability depends on the local channel lineup. • DAZN: Available to subscribers of the Spurs on DAZN streaming package. • Prime Video: Available to subscribers with access to NBA games through Prime Video. • DIRECTV: Channel 680, through the Spurs on DAZN game feed. • AT&T U-verse: Channels 1756 and 756. The free broadcast comes through the Spurs' partnership with Sinclair Broadcast Group, which is bringing 22 games to over-the-air television across San Antonio and South Texas during the 2026-27 season. And Friday's game is just the beginning. After the Warriors matchup, fans will have 20 more opportunities to watch the Spurs for free on CW SA this season. The next two free broadcasts are scheduled for Nov. 17, when San Antonio hosts the Detroit Pistons, and Nov. 25, when the Portland Trail Blazers visit Frost Bank Center. Fans who prefer streaming can subscribe to Spurs on DAZN for $19.99 per month or purchase a season pass for $119.99. Those looking to avoid another monthly bill can tune in to CW SA with an antenna, provided they receive the station's signal. For more information on where to watch Spurs games, fans can visit the team's official broadcast guide at NBA.com/Spurs . Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: Opinion: Pochettino replaces Carrick and my apathy toward Manchester United returns
item.description: MIDDLESBROUGH, ENGLAND - JANUARY 09: Michael Carrick, Manager of Middlesbrough, and Mauricio Pochettino, Manager of Chelsea, shake hands prior to the Carabao Cup Semi Final First Leg match between Middlesbrough and Chelsea at Riverside Stadium on January 09, 2024 in Middlesbrough, England. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re looking for where the vibes are at for Manchester United on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, you better ask Dante to help you find them. Another club legend has unceremoniously been shown the door — the third manager sacked by INEOS in less than two years and three weeks — and the club has confirmed its eighth permanent manager/head coach for the men’s team since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in May 2013. That’s right, Michael Carrick, who took the interim role exactly 11 months ago, coached the team to one of the best second-half of the season records in the Premier League, finished third in the league, and secured Champions League football, is once again forced to take the high road with a classy goodbye post on social media; capping off one final full week of work knowing the ghouls above him were working out the final contract details with another manager whilst he was running training. Michael Carrick dignified as always. pic.twitter.com/V6Bf1plEdE — Simon Stone (@sistoney67) November 13, 2026 But don’t worry everyone, at the expense of Carrick’s love and duty to the club, the decade-long, will-they-won’t-they, with Mauricio Pochettino has finally hard launched, and Manchester United got their man, days before we got Grand Theft Auto VI. The way in which the the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada, and Jason Wilcox handled Carrick’s exit is embarrassing, unprofessional, and one more example of how this club has truly lost its way. My hope, like how I felt when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was sacked , is that Carrick is soon over the disappointment and feels relief to be rid of this shit; swap out the names in the quote below and the sentiment is the exact same for me. Ultimately, Ole conducted himself professionally and with the club and his players, not his own professional ambitions, in the front of his mind. Even in the moments when the things he did failed, I truly believe everything he did was for the betterment of Manchester United and the players, and, in turn, for you, me, us. “ Thank you, Ole ,” by Nathan Heintschel I’m sad, I’m numb, I’m disappointed, and, frankly, I’m shocked that it was only eight months ago that I was finally at my first-ever match at Old Trafford , and I watched in awe as Carrick coached the squad to a 3-1 victory over Aston Villa. So, here we are, the first day of another new era; one day closer to death. The best we can hope for at this point, as the sands of time continue their spiral downward, is for Pochettino to achieve what David Moyes, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim, Carrick, and a smattering of interim appointments could not achieve in

item.title: DeChambeau Details Plans For New Golf Course In California Hometown
item.description: Bryson DeChambeau has disclosed additional details of the golf course community he's planning in his hometown of Clovis, California. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty Images Bryson DeChambeau has partnered with a real estate developer in his hometown of Clovis, California, to create a new residential and lifestyle community called The Orchard Golf Club that pairs championship golf with the region’s rich agricultural heritage. DeChambeau, a two-time U.S. Open champion who attended Clovis East High School and won the California State Junior Championship at age 16, said he feels a “deep responsibility to give back to the region” that has provided him with so much and has been working on regulatory components of the project since 2022. DeChambeau acquired a historic property across the street from his high school, McFarlane Ranch, and is working with Cook Land Company to create the master planned community that will feature an 18-hole golf course and elevated practice facilities. There will also be an on-site farmers market open to the public as well as other community amenities, including programs intended to provide access for kids and schools in the area. “This is a profound opportunity for my team and I to work with the Cook family to help revitalize the area by investing in a project that uses golf to truly serve the community,” DeChambeau said in a press release. DeChambeau said he and his team will design the course and the practice facilities, calling them “the first of many fully procured DeChambeau Designs.” Each hole on the course at The Orchard will be surrounded by a different variety of fruit or nut tree, creating a distinctive experience and highlighting the area’s agricultural ties. A clubhouse and “thoughtfully designed homes” are also part of the plans submitted to the City of Clovis and Fresno County. There is no definitive timetable for the completion of the course or other community components. “The development regulations in California are complex but (the city and county have), and will continue to, work hand in hand to bring this important project to the region,” DeChambeau said in a letter to residents of Clovis, which is about 10 miles northeast of Fresno, and the surrounding Central Valley region. “We anticipate approval within 18 months, with some amenities such as a driving range coming sooner.” A Google Earth image of DeChambeau's high school, Clovis East, and the surrounding area in his California hometown where The Orchard Golf Club is planned. Google Earth After high school in California, DeChambeau attended Southern Methodist University in Dallas, where he majored in physics and won the 2015 NCAA men’s golf individual championship. DeChambeau turned pro in 2016 and won nine PGA Tour titles before joining the Saudi-backed LIV Golf tour in 2022. item.title: Maple Leafs’ Jim Hiller faces questions after Auston Matthews’ postgame revelation
item.description: Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews has raised fresh questions about head coach Jim Hiller’s communication with players after games. Following Thursday’s 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild, Matthews revealed that Hiller usually does not address the team after games. His comments soon sparked criticism from NHL fans and hockey personalities. “He usually doesn’t speak after games, so I’m sure we’ll continue to try to clean some stuff up, go over video and make adjustments,” Matthews said. “At the end of the day, it’s just minimizing those big mistakes or turnovers, especially against other teams’ top lines.” MORE: Maple Leafs under fire as losing skid continues in loss to Avalanche Auston Matthews says head coach Jim Hiller hasn’t been speaking to the team after games: “He usually doesn’t speak after games, so I’m sure we’ll continue to try to clean some stuff up, go over video and make adjustments. At the end of the day, it’s just minimizing those big… pic.twitter.com/kRC2EUH6jY — Leafslatest (@Leafslatest) November 13, 2026 The defeat marked Toronto’s fifth consecutive home loss and extended its losing streak to five games. The Maple Leafs have now lost seven of their last eight games. Matthews also acknowledged the team’s growing confidence problems. “It’s obviously not fun,” Matthews said. “The losses keep piling up. I think the confidence gets shaken a little bit. But it’s just on us as a team, as a group, to fight through it.” Maple Leafs’ Jim Hiller faces growing criticism Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller listens to questions at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Matthews insisted that players must take responsibility rather than blame coaching alone. However, his revelation about postgame communication became a talking point. Draft and Leafs writer Peter Baracchini questioned Hiller’s approach. “ A real coach would, you know , speak after a game. Especially where you lost 5 in a row. Jim Hiller really needs to step it up,” Baracchini wrote. Hockey content creator Mike Bartner also reacted with disbelief, writing, “ AI is getting crazy bc there’s no way this is real, right?” One fan called the situation “ the final nail in Jim Hiller’s casket ,” while online personality David Brown simply wrote, “ Ok Hiller needs to go .” Analyst Peter Berce wrote, “ Jim Hiller doesn’t have the answer from behind the bench. Uninspiring hire, and uninspiring play. Can’t be laid all on the coach, but this team needs a trade. Oh wait, they can’t. They are cooked.” Podcaster Kyle Grimard reacted, “ This is insane. What do you mean he doesn’t speak to the team after games?!? It’s quite literally his job to. Get his *** out of there, holy.” Meanwhile, Matthews delivered a blunt assessment of Toronto’s problems. “We have to stop compounding these big mistakes that end up in the back of our net,” he said. item.title: Barcelona star’s father responds to Serie A links
item.description: Barcelona star’s father responds to Serie A links The father of Barcelona star Hamza Abdelkarim has this week moved to play down any and all speculation linking his client with a move away from the club. Frontman Abdelkarim was over the summer widely tipped to play a prominent role in the first-team setup in Catalunya’s capital this term, after shining under Hansi Flick’s watch during pre-season. To date, however, this has not proven to be the case, with the Egyptian international struggling to carve out minutes for himself amongst Barcelona’s star-studded frontline. Such woes have given rise to recent suggestions that Abdelkarim could be on the move as early as January, in a bid to secure more regular first-team football. This, however, will not prove to be the case. Speaking during an interview with Eram News, as cited by Mundo Deportivo , this week, Mohammed Abdel Karim, Hamza’s father, assured: “What’s being said about Hamza leaving Barcelona isn’t true, and the rumours about his transfer to Como in Italy are fabricated.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: ‘We are not enemies’, Tinubu condemns political violence, warns perpetrators
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎President Bola Tinubu has strongly condemned violence in all its forms and reiterated his earlier directive to security agencies to go after those behind the dastardly acts, irrespective of their political leanings. ‎ ‎President Tinubu, who frowned at the reported resurgence of violence in different parts of the country, said that being in different political parties or pursuing different ambitions does not make political actors enemies. ‎ ‎In a statement he personally issued, titled “Let’s Shun Violence: Our Campaigns Must Be About Issues That Promote the Welfare of Our People,” the President ordered security agencies to confront thuggery and other anti-social and anti-democratic activities with full force. ‎ ‎The statement read: “I have followed recent reports of violence accompanying political events in different parts of the country. ‎ ‎“Every form of violence is condemned. Violence should never have a place in our political campaigns as we move toward the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎“Our campaigns should be about issues—a contestation of ideas that promotes the welfare of our people and the progress of our country. ‎ ‎“As the leader of this country, I commit myself to a peaceful, free, and fair election, and I urge political leaders and supporters across party lines to conduct themselves responsibly. ‎ ‎“I have said that being in different political parties or pursuing different ambitions does not make us enemies. ‎ ‎“As Nigerians, we are members of the same household living in different rooms. Therefore, our politics must elevate human conditions and focus on national progress and development. ‎ ‎“I want to reiterate my previous directive to the security agencies: be strict and firm against anyone who seeks to test our resolve and will to preserve public order.” ‎ ‎President Tinubu said his administration is committed to an orderly and peaceful election, adding that all political parties and candidates should be protected and free to campaign anywhere in the country without molestation or fear for their safety. ‎ ‎“We shall not tolerate any irresponsible conduct by politicians and their supporters,” he said. ‎ ‎The President further added: “Security agencies are therefore authorised to confront thuggery and other anti-social and anti-democratic activities with full force.” ‎ The post ‘We are not enemies’, Tinubu condemns political violence, warns perpetrators appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Explained: Nigeria’s chances of qualifying for AFCON 2027 after beating Tanzania
item.description: Nigeria have boosted their chances of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON after defeating Tanzania 3-1 in their latest qualifying fixture at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday. The victory moved the Super Eagles to second place in Group L with six points, just one point behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have seven points. Madagascar occupy third position with two points, while Tanzania sit bottom with one point. However, Nigeria still have work to do to secure their place at the tournament, as only one additional qualification ticket is available in the group. Tanzania have already secured their place at AFCON 2027 as one of the three co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda. This means Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar are competing for the group’s remaining qualification spot. Current Group L standings Position Country Points 1 Guinea-Bissau 7 2 Nigeria 6 3 Madagascar 2 4 Tanzania 1 What Nigeria need to qualify 1. Win their remaining matches Nigeria must continue collecting maximum points in their remaining fixtures to strengthen their chances of finishing top of the group. The Super Eagles have three qualifying matches left, including their return fixture against Tanzania on Tuesday, November 17. A victory would keep them within touching distance of Guinea-Bissau and put additional pressure on the group leaders. 2. Overtake Guinea-Bissau Guinea-Bissau remain Nigeria’s biggest obstacle in the qualification race. With seven points, they currently enjoy a one-point advantage over the Super Eagles. Nigeria must finish above them to secure the group’s only available qualification ticket. 3. Watch Guinea-Bissau’s remaining fixtures Guinea-Bissau’s results in their remaining matches, particularly against Madagascar, could have a significant impact on Nigeria’s qualification chances. Any dropped points by the group leaders would present the Super Eagles with an opportunity to move to the top of the standings. 4. Win the decisive March fixtures After their November encounter against Tanzania, Nigeria will have two more qualifying matches in March 2027. The Super Eagles are scheduled to travel to face Madagascar before hosting Guinea-Bissau in their final group fixture. The two matches could ultimately determine Nigeria’s fate, particularly the home encounter against Guinea-Bissau, which may become a decisive battle for the group’s qualification ticket. When will Nigeria’s qualification be decided? The remaining qualifying fixtures will be played in November 2026 and March 2027. Nigeria’s immediate assignment is the return fixture against Tanzania on Tuesday, November 17. They will then face Madagascar away before welcoming Guinea-Bissau in March 2027 to conclude their qualifying campaign. The Super Eagles will be hoping to enter those final fixtures in a strong position and avoid depending on other results to secure qualification. item.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
item.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. An alumna of Yale University (where she earned her B.A.) and Yale Law School (where she earned her J.D.), Emehelu is a proud resident of Montclair, New Jersey, where she and her husband, Ike , raised their two children, Nnamdi and Amara . item.title: AFCONQ: Arokodare scores brace as Super Eagles defeat Tanzania 3-1
item.description: The Super Eagles of Nigeria bounced back to winning ways in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON qualifying campaign with a 3-1 victory over Tanzania at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday. Nigeria took an early lead through Alhassan Yusuf, who found the back of the net in the third minute to give the hosts a promising start. However, Tanzania fought back and restored parity in the 36th minute after Wilfred Ndidi lost possession in midfield, allowing Msanga to capitalise on slack defending and make it 1-1. The Super Eagles suffered another setback before the break when Ademola Lookman was forced off with an injury and replaced by Moses Simon. Both teams went into half-time level, with Nigeria seeking to regain their advantage after the restart. Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle introduced Tolu Arokodare and Chidera Usor at the beginning of the second half, replacing Alhassan Yusuf and Raphael Onyedika. The changes paid off as Arokodare restored Nigeria’s lead in the 52nd minute with an excellent flicked finish to make it 2-1. The striker completed his brace in the 60th minute, finishing off a move created by fellow substitute Nsor to extend Nigeria’s advantage to 3-1. Chelle’s men maintained their two-goal cushion in the closing stages, although Arokodare missed an opportunity to complete his hat-trick. The final whistle confirmed a 3-1 victory for Nigeria, giving the Super Eagles a boost in their quest for qualification for the 2027 AFCON.
