item.title: 'Martian Isolation' is an upcoming sci-fi survival horror game that looks like 'The Martian' and 'Event Horizon' had a horrific child
item.description: null "Martian Isolation" is an upcoming single-player, first-person survival horror game that's just been revealed with a suitably creepy launch trailer. And yes, it does look an awful lot like " The Martian ," doesn't it? There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base. That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls. Oh yeah, that's some good creepy sci-fi horror right there. It's giving " Event Horizon ", and that's always getting a thumbs-up from me. There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027". You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist. Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging. There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike. The psychological torment only begins once the sun goes down (they mostly come out at night … mostly), as your character starts encountering cosmic horrors and weird naked zombie men. Mars rover, nice. Golden Milestone Studio Spacesuits, check. Golden Milestone Studio Crafting, of course. Golden Milestone Studio OH SWEET JESUS! Get it away, get it away. Golden Milestone Studio OK, we're good. Mining, cool. Golden Milestone Studio Riding a quad bike on Mars, yes please. Golden Milestone Studio Growing potatoes on Mars, just like that guy in the movie. Golden Milestone Studio Opening a box with power tools, seems excessive but sure. Golden Milestone Studio NOPE! Nope, nope, nope, I'm out! Golden Milestone Studio Are they hallucinations, or is there some malevolent presence hiding in the blood-red sands of Mars ? I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish " Routine ." I left my character hiding under a desk months ago, and I haven't been brave enough to go back. As Mama always said, you can't have any Martian horror until you finish your lunar horror first.

item.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes rejects second contract offer
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected the club’s second offer to extend his contract, leaving negotiations over the Portugal midfielder’s future unresolved. BBC Sport reports that Fernandes is out of contract at the end of the season, although United can extend his deal by 12 months, until 2028. The club wants to agree a new contract before using that option. If no agreement is reached, United are expected to trigger the extension before January 1. Without it, Fernandes would be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs from that date, with six months remaining on his deal. It is unclear when Fernandes rejected the offer. A resolution does not appear imminent amid the upheaval at Old Trafford: Michael Carrick was sacked on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to take over as head coach. United will hope Pochettino’s arrival can persuade Fernandes to stay. The midfielder came close to joining Pochettino’s Tottenham in 2019, before moving from Sporting to United six months later. He has scored six goals in 13 appearances for United this season. BBC chief football news reporter Simon Stone says Fernandes wants to compete for the biggest prizes and will want to see what impact Pochettino has at United. The club, meanwhile, must weigh the cost and length of a new deal against Fernandes’ recent drop in form after an outstanding previous season, when he broke the Premier League assists record and won major player-of-the-year awards. Fernandes is 32, and a new contract could commit United to a substantial outlay over several years. Both sides may therefore have reasons to take their time, despite the club’s wish to keep its captain. item.title: Meet the US family with five generations born on the same date
item.description: An American family has entered the Guinness World Records after five consecutive generations were born on the same date, September 14, in a remarkable family coincidence spanning more than a century. The Bell and Harlow family secured the record for the most generations born on the same day after the arrival of baby Arthur Bell on September 14, 2025. Arthur’s birth extended a family tradition that began with his great-great-grandfather, Wilber Harlow, who was born on September 14, 1907. The other family members who share the birthday are Wilber’s daughter, Addie Harlow, born on September 14, 1949; his grandson, Donald Harlow, born on September 14, 1972; and his great-granddaughter, Emma Bell, born on September 14, 1997. Emma is Arthur’s mother, while Donald is his grandfather. According to Guinness World Records, the family surpassed the previous record of four generations born on the same date, which had been jointly held by seven families. The family said they had been aware of the unusual coincidence when four generations shared the September 14 birthday but delayed applying for official recognition because they hoped another child would continue the tradition. Their wish came true when Emma’s second child, Arthur, arrived on the expected date, extending the record to five generations. Speaking about the achievement, Emma said the family had always known they could hold the record but wanted to wait until they had a fifth generation. “We kind of always knew that we held a record with four generations, we just never applied because we had that ambition to have the fifth on 14 September,” she said. “And then it worked out!” She added that the family was delighted to become the sole record holders rather than share the title with other families. Arthur’s grandfather, Donald, also expressed his excitement, saying: “God works in beautiful ways.” The family’s birthday tradition began in 1907 when Wilber Harlow was born. He later worked as a postmaster and owned the Harlow General Store in Brooks, Iowa. On September 14, 1949, Wilber and his wife welcomed their daughter, Addie, on his birthday, beginning the remarkable sequence. Addie later worked as a secretary for the Chief of Police in La Vista, Nebraska, for more than 20 years. Her son, Donald, continued the coincidence when he was born on the same date in 1972. Donald subsequently welcomed Emma, who also arrived on September 14, 1997. Although Addie died in 2023 before Arthur’s birth, the family had maintained the tradition of celebrating their shared birthday together, usually by visiting a restaurant and having a birthday cake. Emma and her husband, Wyatt, said they became particularly excited when they realised their second child’s expected arrival date was September 14. The family also noticed another unusual pattern in the sequence: the five generations alternate between boys and girls, following a boy-girl-boy-girl-boy pattern. item.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
item.description: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Read full article Comments

item.title: U-23 AFCONQ: Nigeria suffer 2-0 defeat to DR Congo in first leg
item.description: Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations suffered a setback on Friday after the Olympic Eagles lost 2-0 to DR Congo in the first leg of their second-round qualifying tie. The Nigerian side, led by Ikorodu City head coach Bright Osehai Ozebagbe and former Nigeria U-20 assistant coach Deniran Ortega, struggled to convert their early opportunities as the hosts secured a comfortable advantage ahead of the return fixture. The coaching duo took charge in the absence of Super Eagles manager Eric Chelle, who was occupied with Nigeria’s senior national team preparations for their crucial Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. Nigeria started brightly and nearly took the lead in the fourth minute when Victor Samuel’s effort missed the target. The midfielder had another opportunity five minutes later after finding himself one-on-one with the DR Congo goalkeeper but failed to convert. The missed chances proved costly as DR Congo took the lead in the 20th minute in controversial circumstances. Nigeria goalkeeper Samuel James appeared to have been fouled by a Congolese player while attempting to collect an aerial ball during the build-up to the opening goal. However, the referee allowed the goal to stand. The Olympic Eagles suffered another setback in the 30th minute when Brighton youngster Zadok Yohanna was forced off with an injury. DR Congo doubled their advantage five minutes before the break through Felozefe Mabete, who produced an impressive free-kick to put the hosts firmly in control. Despite their attempts to find a way back into the contest after the restart, Nigeria could not break down the Congolese defence, with the hosts protecting their two-goal advantage until the final whistle. The result leaves the Olympic Eagles with a difficult task in the second leg, as they must overturn the deficit to keep their qualification hopes alive. Nigeria will host DR Congo in the return fixture at the Remo Stars Stadium on Tuesday, where they will seek to secure an aggregate victory and advance to the final qualifying round. The Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations also serves as the qualification pathway for the men’s football tournament at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. item.title: Boko Haram: Zulum announces ₦50k for each soldier deployed to Borno communities
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities of Maiwa and Koshebe villages. Our Correspondent report that Koshebe in November 28, 2020 came under massacre when some armed Boko Haram militants launched a devastating attack on peasant and laborer rice farmers working in the fields (near Zabarmari and Maiduguri), where over 100 farm laborers—many of whom traveled from Sokoto State in northwest Nigeria for seasonal harvest work—were rounded up, tied, and their throats slit. Likewise, in November, 2023, suspected Boko Haram insurgents again targeted rice farmers harvesting crops in the Karkut and Koshebe general areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 farmers and leaving others missing. But Zulum assured that he will provide the needed support to strengthen security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, ensure safe travel, and revive trade in communities recovering from years of insurgency. The Governor gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. The highway links communities along the corridor to markets and facilitates the movement of agricultural produce, essential commodities and other goods. Zulum said improving security along the route would help residents travel safely, trade and rebuild their livelihoods. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe villages, the governor pledged “to provide operational logistics and sustain welfare support. He announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities”. Governor Zulum’s administration has consistently supported military operations with logistics and welfare assistance as part of efforts to improve security and help displaced residents return to their communities. The Governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. item.title: Stephen King and Real-Life Serial Killers Shaped the Most Unhinged Thriller of 2026

Directed by Zachary Wigon ( Sanctuary ) and based on the Virginia Feito novel, the movie is set in the mid-1800s, our most hysterical era, and follows Winifred Notty (Monroe), a newly hired governess who arrives at a gothic manor to tutor the Pounds’ children (Jacobi Jupe and Evie Templeton). item.title: Astronomers trace mystery radio signals back to cosmic odd couple of white dwarf and sun-like star
item.description: null Astronomers have traced a mysterious radio signal back to a cosmic odd couple comprised of a dead star, a white dwarf, and its stellar companion, a sun-like star. The white dwarf in the newly discovered system, designated GPM J071507−114153 and located around 5,000 light-years away, spins once every eight minutes, sending out radio pulses. These radio pulses have been seen from binary systems with smaller and cooler red dwarf stars before, but rarely from a system like GPM J071507−114153. GPM J071507−114153 belongs to a class of celestial objects called long-period transients (LPTs) known to produce radio signals that switch on and off over intervals of minutes or hours. Around a dozen LPTs have been detected since the team behind this research found the first in 2021. Several previously discovered LPT systems contain a white dwarf and a companion star, but it has been unclear which of the two stars was generating the radio pulses. That means the discovery of GPM J071507−114153 and finding that the pulses come from close to the white dwarf could be a significant step toward understanding the nature of LPTs. The unusual system consists of a small and highly energetic white dwarf pulsar, orbiting a much larger star similar to our sun. (Image credit: ICRAR) "This is the first time the pulses are clear enough to see the white dwarf moving in its orbit around its companion," team leader and commissioning scientist with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKA), Sam McSweeney, said in a statement . "So we know that the pulsations are coming from a region close to the white dwarf, or possibly even from the white dwarf itself." The pulses seen by the team also allowed them to detect stellar flares erupting on the sun-like star. "As a bonus, we also saw the white dwarf moving behind a region with a strong magnetic field, most likely a 'stellar prominence,' which is a large loop of plasma erupting from a star's surface," team member Natasha Hurley-Walker of the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research (ICRAR), Curtin University, Australia, said. "It's amazing that by using radio wavelengths we can detect the storms on a star over 5,000 light-years away." South Africa’s MeerKAT telescope. (Image credit: South African Radio Astronomy Observatory (SARAO)) Hurley-Walker and the team at ICRAR have been at the cutting edge of rare star systems like this. "We detected this system in a large survey using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) to scan the entire Milky Way visible from Australia," Hurley-Walker said. "We then used the MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa to determine its precise position." After the radio telescopes detected this LPT, it was confirmed using the W.M. Keck Observatory on Maunakea in Hawaii. The visible light follow-up of Keck also confirmed that the star in GPM J071507−114153 was a G-type star, just like the sun. item.title: Mozilla leaves Solo website owners to go it alone as hosting shuts down
item.description: Solo, Mozilla's LLM-powered website builder and hosting service, is shutting down. All sites and data will be deleted on November 30. Mozilla launched Solo in December 2023 as a "Mozilla Innovation Project," aimed at helping sole traders to build themselves a webpage for their services. S ome 54,000 people used its LLM to build pages, and relied on Mozilla to host them – complete with custom domain names. Well, not any more. Now the Soloist.ai homepage says: "We've made the difficult decision to close Solo. We have appreciated all of your support building and growing this product, and the feedback we've received from all of you. Solo will cease operations on Nov 30, 2026." Users now have just over two weeks left to find a new home for their pages, although Mozilla says it first notified them on October 1. According to the support FAQ , users can download a ZIP containing an HTML export, contact form and newsletter submissions, and a CSV linking to their images. The images themselves must be downloaded separately. Domains purchased through Solo Domains must also be moved to Name.com , with Mozilla handling the transfer after users create an account and supply its code. So much for having the fiddly bits taken care of. It also points at a couple of other bot-based site-generating services – in case all this feels like a bit too much. We suspect that for the sort of technophobes that this was aimed at, it very probably will. Mozilla told The Register : "Experimentation is an important part of Mozilla's mission to make the internet better and give people more choice and control online. Sometimes, that means making the decision to bring a product to an end. Solo will officially shut down on November 30, 2026. We initially notified customers on October 1, providing a 60-day transition period, and have been offering support to help them download their website data and migrate their domains purchased via Solo Domains to another hosting provider." It seems that some 54,000 users were not enough to keep it going, and we can see that this would cost money to keep running. An HTML export is a start, though the FAQ doesn't explain how much work it will take to get a complete, functioning site running elsewhere. Buried in the dark recesses of the web is this vulture's own nearly 30-year-old homepage, created using a mixture of Claris Home Page (which was excellent) and Microsoft FrontPage (ever so slightly less so). We saw what a mess machine-generated web content was back then, and thanks to LLMs, we suspect it is almost infinitely worse now. Mozilla might have made a few bucks by finding a commercial partner to take on its users, and perhaps through them offer a paid site-and-domain transfer service. As we noted last year, it seems not to have negotiated anything with KaiOSTech, which maintains and sells what used to be the formerly FOSS FirefoxOS for use on low-end smartphones.

item.title: Conversion to university: We are waiting for release of government gazette – Abdul, YABATECH Rector
item.description: By Adesina Wahab The conversion of Yaba College of Technology, YABATECH, to the Federal University of Technology and Vocational Studies is being delayed because the Federal Government is yet to release the official gazette that would convey that, the Rector, Dr Ibraheem Abdul, has disclosed. He stated this on Friday while answering questions on the sideline of the press briefing to herald the 38th convocation ceremonies of the College. “We are pretty much on course to becoming a University. The bill has been passed by the National Assembly and it has been signed into law by President Bola Tinubu. At our end, we are adequately prepared. What remains now is for the official gazette to be released by the Federal Government. When that is done, the institutional evaluation will be conducted by the Federal Ministry of Education and then the National Universities Commission, NUC, would come and accredit our courses. “Indeed, this historic conversion reflects the growing recognition by the President and the larger society of the importance of technology-driven and Vocational education in addressing Nigeria’s human-capital and industrial development needs,” he said. As part of the convocation ceremonies, Dr Abdul said the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, the Minister of Finance, Mr Taiwo Oyedele and Mrs Itunu Omotayo would be conferred Fellowship of the College. Also, Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Hamzat, will deliver the convocation lecture titled ” From silos to synergy: Reimagining Nigeria’s tertiary education system for national transformation”. The event will be chaired by the Minister of State for Education, Prof.Suwaiba Ahmad. Giving a breakdown of the number of graduating students, the Rector said a total of 10,886 would be involved. Out of the figure, 361 are graduating with distinction, 3,160 earned upper credit pass, 5,696 are graduating with lower credit pass and 1,669 have pass grade. Abdul added that the College has continued to promote entrepreneurship as an essential component of its education philosophy and that the citing of the Folawiyo Entrepreneurship Centre in the College was a testament to that . The post Conversion to university: We are waiting for release of government gazette – Abdul, YABATECH Rector appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Email addresses used in European school bomb hoaxes spotted in old infostealer logs
item.description: Two email addresses used to send bomb threats that disrupted thousands of Italian schools this week were found exposed in infostealer logs for over a year, experts say. Researchers at Hudson Rock looked into the two university email addresses used to send the bomb threats. One, from Egypt’s Kafrelsheikh University, was scooped up by Vidar – a cybercrime tool that steals saved account credentials and passwords from an infected computer and leaks them to attackers – as far back as October 2021. The other, from Taiwan's Dayeh University, was found among the 284 million addresses included in the massive AlienTXTBASE infostealer dump , dated February 2025. The experts said that the two addresses in infostealer logs do not strictly mean that those behind the bomb threats gained access to the accounts using the previous infostealer compromise. However, it suggests that there was ample time for the universities and Microsoft, which both universities used for authentication, to take action against the accounts that they should have been aware were appearing in infostealer logs. Modern threat intelligence has made infostealer logs highly visible. "Both findings place credential exposure well before the disruption, creating a substantial window in which exposed access could have been investigated and secured," Hudson Rock said . The researchers said that they would need access to details such as the email headers, and data from email providers, including sign-in events and audit records, that could show them more about who sent the email and from what session. Understanding whether the sender authenticated into the account could rule out spoofing, but would not in itself provide proof that the sender used a corresponding password taken from an infostealer log, Hudson Rock noted. There are many ways to get around password-based authentication . The researchers said that in any case where a credential is detected among infostealer logs, the organizations responsible for those accounts must contain them, revoke their access, rotate secrets, and go looking for suspicious activity. "The disruption illustrates why credential exposure deserves attention beyond fraud and data theft," the researchers said. "An account associated with an ordinary university user can become a means of reaching schools, frightening families, and consuming emergency resources." The threats Around 6,300 of Italy's 7,476 state schools received fake bomb threat emails between November 11-12, although only around 390 of them evacuated their respective buildings. The emails contained messaging such as "we will annihilate you," and "we will carry out genocide against Italians," and mention of a "powerful explosive device… with a remote trigger." Early reports suggested that the emails came from a Taiwanese email address and were signed by a "Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan" – a fictitious state or region roughly mapping to "the land of Misogyny," with "vilayat" meaning

item.title: FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners. The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas. Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them. Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day. “When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.” A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node. The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says. The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration. Home mining is not a profit play Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III’s debut in February, when FutureBit introduced the hardware as a way for individuals to run both a miner and a node at home. item.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
item.description: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates. item.title: HPE debuts hybrid storage configs: Rising SSD costs hit supercomputing
item.description: HPE is pitching high performance compute customers with hybrid configurations of its Cray Supercomputing Storage Systems built for faster throughput, along with a Rack Management Controller that monitors cooling systems. The hardware giant already supplies its Cray Supercomputing Storage Systems E2000 in all-flash, all-disk, tiered and hybrid configurations, but - we're told - the latest combination offers up to 41 percent more data throughput per storage rack. The E2000 line embeds the Lustre open-source parallel file system, and is generally intended to fit NVMe Gen 5 solid-state drive (SSD) building blocks. For the refreshed hybrid configurations, HPE is combining SSDs with new 32 TB SAS-4 (24 Gb/s SAS) HDDs and new enclosures supporting 74 or 100 drives. HPE says it'll deliver up to 116 GB/s of read throughput and 92 GB/s of write throughput per rack, with up to 32 percent more usable storage capacity per rack for expansion to support the growing size of datasets in HPC, especially where sites are mixing AI and traditional simulation-style workloads. One of the reasons behind these new hybrid configurations could be the ballooning cost of storage, caused by the relentless demand for AI infrastructure skewing the price of components such as memory and many other things. But prices for silicon-based NAND flash SSDs are growing faster than those of good old hard drives , as our colleagues at Blocks & Files reported. HPE says that as demand for data-intensive workloads grows, prices for large SSDs have soared. The company claims the new hybrid configurations let research institutions and national laboratories spend less on storage and put that money toward compute node purchases, without giving up on the performance they need. “When making long-term investments in environments where advanced workloads are rapidly evolving, our customers want scalable, dense, and flexible systems to help them address dynamic shifts in requirements," said Trish Damkroger, HPE senior veep for HPC and AI Infrastructure Solutions. The latest hybrid configurations are expected to go on sale in early 2027. HPE's other introduction is a Rack Management Controller, providing what HPE calls "intelligent liquid cooling” via real-time monitoring, leak detection and automated control features. It integrates with HPE Supercomputing Management Software to gather telemetry and provide control. Several platform-specific versions will be offered, each tailored to different rack-scale systems. Support will launch with HPE's own Cray Supercomputing GX5000 infrastructure, naturally, with versions for Nvidia’s NVL72 and AMD’s Helion and Helios kit to follow. The Rack Management Controller will be available for HPE’s kit in March 2027, with support for AMD and Nvidia expected to follow in June. ®

item.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in alleged $4.5bn fraud trial
item.description: An Ikeja Special Offences Court on Friday admitted a certified copy of a Supreme Court judgment linking former CBN Governor, Godwin Emefiele, to forfeited properties. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. The Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo (SAN), had tendered the document through EFCC investigator, Mr Alvan Gurumnaan. However, Emefiele’s lead counsel, Mr Ojo Olalekan (SAN), opposed its admissibility, arguing that only four justices signed the judgment. He maintained that Supreme Court decisions were ordinarily delivered by panels of five or seven justices. Ojo also argued that the judgment arose from non-conviction forfeiture proceedings and was irrelevant to the prosecution’s case. Counsel to Omoile, Mr Adeyinka Kotoye (SAN), aligned himself with the objections and urged the court to reject the document. Kotoye argued that admitting the judgment could undermine the principle of estoppel and the defendants’ presumption of innocence. He also questioned the prosecution’s decision to introduce the document after proceedings had begun. Responding, Oyedepo argued that the document was a duly certified Supreme Court decision admissible under Sections 102 and 104 of the Evidence Act. Following the ruling, Gurumnaan faced cross-examination by Emefiele’s counsel over his role in the investigation. The witness said he personally obtained statements, analysed bank statements and coordinated other members of the investigation team. He confirmed interviewing Zenith Bank Managing Director, Dr Ebenezer Onyeagwu, but could not immediately recall whether a statement was obtained. Gurumnaan said the investigation involved hundreds of interviews with CBN officials, commercial bank employees and personnel of other government agencies. Oshodi adjourned the case until Dec. 17 for continuation of cross-examination. The

item.title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
item.description: NASA astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. captured this image of the area surrounding the Red Sea and Nile river valley on November 14, 1966, during their four-day mission in space. Gemini XII was the final flight of NASA’s Gemini Program. NASA Astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. orbited Earth from November 11 to 15, 1966, on Gemini XII , the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. In addition to successfully completing rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures vital to sending American astronauts to the Moon, the crew was also spurring the development of a different field of exploration, observing Earth from space. The photos taken by Lovell, Aldrin, and other Gemini astronauts demonstrated the value of orbital imagery for studying Earth’s surface. Their images helped scientists make the case for a dedicated Earth observation satellite program. One of strongest advocates for accelerating the use of Earth-observing satellites was William T. Pecora, the director of the United States Geological Survey from 1965 to 1971. In a 1969 statement, Pecora noted that the Earth Resources Observation Satellite (EROS) program he championed, and which later paved the way for Landsat , was “conceived in 1966 largely as a direct result of the demonstrated utility of Mercury and Gemini orbital photography to Earth resource studies.” For more than five decades, Landsat and other Earth-observing satellites have provided invaluable data used around the world to monitor crops, wildfires, flooding, vegetation health, land use, and countless other changes to our planet. item.title: Netflix’s ‘Ray Gunn’ gets 2nd trailer, and we're hyped for this animated sci-fi noir from ‘Incredibles’ director Brad Bird
item.description: null Dreaming of a bright and shiny future filled with personal jet packs, levitating autos, and automated gadgets straight out of " The Jetsons ?" Add in a gritty mystery, a notorious private eye, double-crossing aliens, and a bombshell diva framed for a killing, and you’ve got the perfect recipe for "Ray Gunn." Oscar-winning director Brad Bird ("The Incredibles," "Ratatouille") returns to our screens with his new big-budget animated sci-fi project, " Ray Gunn ," and this latest trailer has us primed. "In Metropia, a gigantic city in an alternate future as seen from 1939, private eye Raymond Gunn (Sam Rockwell) is drawn into a case involving aliens, murder, and a multimedia starlet named Venus Nova (Scarlett Johansson)," states the official synopsis. Netflix Films and Skydance Animation's "Ray Gunn" is a stylistic pastiche of classic film noir tropes populated by down-and-out detectives and femme fatales living in the inspiring air of technological optimism viewed through a pre-war America lens. Think "The Fifth Element" meets "Who Framed Roger Rabbit?" and "The Maltese Falcon," and you’re going to be close to this sci-fi whodunnit's vibe, which is intended for more mature audiences and rated PG. "The Incredibles'" Brad Bird serves up a sci-fi detective tale in "Ray Gunn" (Image credit: Netflix) This energetic new preview is locked and loaded with dazzling visuals by Cinesite, freaky creatures, streamlined flying cars, and a blistering pace. And if you listen very closely, The B-52s' "Planet Claire" can be heard playing in the background, which is one of the touchstones that inspired Bird to begin his 36-year journey to bring "Ray Gunn" to life. Was it worth the wait? We'll have to find out. Also starring the vocal talents of Tom Waits, Bobby Cannavale, Alan Tudyk, Matt Berry, and Michelle Rodriguez, "Ray Gunn" opens in select theaters and 70mm screenings Dec. 4. After that, it lands on Netflix on Dec. 18... a date you might want to circle on your calendar, as that’s also the release slot for " Avengers: Doomsday " and " Dune: Part 3. " It's going to be a busy day for sci-fi fans. "Strap in, buster!" Watch Ray Gunn on Netflix on Dec 18: Standard with ads: $8.99/month Standard: $19.99/month Premium (4K): $26.99/month

item.title: Microsoft outage gives customers a crash course in dependence on Redmond
item.description: Microsoft 365 services are slowly recovering from a prolonged outage that has handed critics of single-vendor dependence a particularly unwelcome case study. Ever wondered what it would be like if your IT supplier abruptly pulled the plug? Perhaps the result of a mood swing by an unpredictable political leader? For affected Microsoft customers, the disruption has offered an unwelcome preview. Email? Gone. Messaging with Teams? Iffy. Collaboration? Nope. The list of problems in what Microsoft delicately called a "Service Degradation" is breathtaking. The company put the incident's start at 1826 GMT on November 12. Exchange Online fell over. Viewing recently used files in the Microsoft 365 application was problematic. Copilot threw a wobbly. Microsoft 365 Education was affected (unfortunate, considering the changes the company has made ), and so on. At 1401 GMT on November 13, Microsoft reported: "We're continuing to see improvements in service availability," but the damage has surely been done. If the outage halted work at your organization, then questions will have to be asked. Even Microsoft's rivals had some sympathy for the engineers and administrators dealing with the problems. Jos Poortvliet, co-founder of Nextcloud, told The Register : "Mistakes happen in the IT industry. This holds true for companies of all sizes, including us. Our heart goes out to all the admins today. "This incident shows how dependent organizations are on a single ecosystem. Especially in critical infrastructure, monopolies are increasing the risk of stalling businesses globally if an incident occurs. "When everything is hanging on a single vendor, companies can't switch providers quickly to get back up and running, or have a second setup as backup, or pull the plug when under attack and keep working air-gapped." Similarly, Civo CEO Mark Boost noted that IT whoopsies were a way of life. "Every technology provider will experience failures," he said. "The real concern isn't that Microsoft has suffered an outage. It's that we've allowed so much of our critical infrastructure to become concentrated in the hands of so few companies, creating enormous single points of failure." Dame Chi Onwurah, chair of the Commons Science and Technology Committee, also commented: "The global Microsoft outage only serves to highlight once again the lack of resilience in the UK's digital infrastructure, and the dangers that this dependency can pose to our security, economy and public services." This week, Microsoft warned users to treat its unsupported Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 as " permanently vulnerable ." Moving to Exchange Online brings its own dependencies, however. Beyond any compensation claims, Microsoft may face awkward conversations about those dependencies when contracts come up for renewal. And there are alternatives. Although perhaps not so extreme as the measures overheard by one vulture in a German shared workspace: "Germany's love of the fax machine – we are finally getti

item.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. The matter also attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), which arraigned her over alleged offences connected to the fundraising campaign. She pleaded not guilty to the charges. Vanguard News The post Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Jaji wins Zamfara APC rerun primary with 26,646 votes
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The incumbent member representing Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency of Zamfara State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) court-ordered fresh primary election with 26,646 votes. Jaji defeated two other aspirants in the rerun conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, to reclaim the party’s ticket after his earlier nomination was nullified by the Federal High Court in Abuja. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the exercise, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the Kaura Namoda Collation Centre after the conclusion of voting and collation across the two local government areas. According to the committee, the constituency had 42,266 registered APC members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited, while 27,359 votes were recorded as total votes cast. Jaji’s closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, polled 713 votes, while the third contestant, Musa Zubairu, failed to secure any vote. A breakdown of the results showed that Jaji won in both local government areas, polling 14,264 votes in Kaura Namoda against Dangaladima’s 465, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji, Jaji secured 12,382 votes, compared with Dangaladima’s 248 votes, while Zubairu again failed to record any vote. Declaring the results, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and the party’s guidelines governing primary elections. “Having satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and guidelines, I hereby declare Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji the winner of the fresh primary election,” he announced. The rerun followed a legal challenge instituted by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court in Abuja against Jaji’s earlier emergence as the party’s candidate for the constituency. The court nullified the earlier nomination and directed the APC to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The party’s national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the exercise in compliance with the court’s directive. Jaji, who is associated with the political camp of the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has now secured the party’s ticket through the court-ordered process. The outcome settles the party’s immediate nomination contest in the constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the legal dispute over its earlier primary election. item.title: Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double Crypto trading on Robinhood fell by almost half from a year ago in October, the company said Thursday , as customers traded $17 billion of digital assets while their bets on event contracts more than doubled. The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025. Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year. Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025. Event contracts take off as crypto cools The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts. Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms. The rest of Robinhood’s brokerage held up better than crypto. Equity notional volume rose 2% from a year earlier to $325 billion, and options contracts traded climbed 8% to 289 million. Margin balances reached $22.9 billion, up 39% year over year. Funded customers rose by about 130,000 in the month to 28.9 million, and net deposits came to $15.1 billion. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier. Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. The release, like all of the company’s monthly updates, is unaudited and preliminary. Retail pulls back as bitcoin slides The slump in Robinhood’s crypto numbers lines up with a broader retreat by retail traders. Bitcoin ended September near $83,500 and has slid since, falling below $70,000 early Friday for the first time since August as a hot inflation report raised bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Institutional demand has cooled alongside it. U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted a sixth straight day of net outflows on Thursday, and BlackRock’s IBIT, the largest of them, bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday. item.title: Another Linux kernel developer steps back from some duties due to overload
item.description: Arm's Lorenzo Stoakes isn't quitting Linux kernel development, though he's stepping back from some of the patch-review work he used to handle. Stoakes is a principal software engineer at Arm and he's a busy chap. Aside from writing the forthcoming book The Linux Memory Manager , in his CV [PDF], he says: "I hold four maintainerships: memory mapping, memory mapping (locking), memory mapping (madvise) – essentially the entirety of the userland API to memory management – and the reverse mapping which connects physical to virtual memory." Even so, he plans to soon be doing a little less. Earlier this week he posted an email to the Linux kernel mailing list to say that he was planning to drop some of his workload. He explained: "Given the current throughput in the kernel resulting from AI-generated series, I unfortunately lack the bandwidth to generally be able to offer review except in those areas I maintain. […] Apologies for doing this, but given the current trends I'd like to do something to make my inbox a little more manageable." As it happens, this came just the day after the Paramount Penguin himself said that he saw signs that the AI patch tide was "starting to turn." Stoakes told The Register : "I am retaining my maintainerships and have no plans on giving those up, I just want my inbox to be less horrendous. "And yeah, AI is part of the reason; in general, it's gone from 'once a week' to 'daily' to 'half of what I see in review'. "But the AI wave is hitting [memory management] across the board, really." He added: "I have a habit of burning myself out over weekends and evenings – you can see my involvement on a thread talking about that here - which gives you a sense of my views if you read back through that thread." At the Open Source Summit last month, the Reg FOSS desk joined the "Ask the Expert" session with Greg Kroah-Hartman , and he too expressed worrying sentiments: "The onslaught of the LLM-generated patches… we don't have enough people to review them all… We need more reviewers. We don't have enough. All of the maintainers are burnt out, and we have been for ten years." Kroah-Hartman also said: "I want to go down to two Long Term Support releases – four, maximum. Six is too many. We're too busy. We don't have the manpower. It’s crazy." On Red Hat's model of offering 10 years of support for products with a given version of the kernel: "Debian does it right. Debian and Yocto run the world. I've argued for years that the RHEL and SLES model is broken. That's why I don't work for SUSE any more." ®

item.title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences
item.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Report No fewer than 53 Nigerians were among 112 undocumented African nationals arrested by Malaysian immigration authorities between January and October 31 over various immigration offences, Malaysian newspaper, Utusan Malaysia, has reported. The Nigerians recorded the highest number of arrests among the African nationals, followed by Uganda with 13, Kenya with 10 and Ghana with eight. The Director-General of Malaysia’s Immigration Department, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, disclosed the figures in an interview with Utusan Malaysia, published on Friday. According to the report, other nationals arrested included Somalia (6), Tanzania (6), Senegal (4), Algeria (3), Burkina Faso (2), Togo (2) and The Gambia (2). One national each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also arrested. Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, contrary to Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. He said 85 people were arrested for the offence, including 47 Nigerians. “The primary offence recorded is entering and remaining in the country without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63; this resulted in 85 arrests, 47 of which involved Nigerian nationals,” he said. The immigration chief said 23 others were arrested for overstaying their permitted period under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act. He added that three people were detained for violating the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested for allegedly possessing forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act. The authorities also arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid immigration passes. Shaaban said the enforcement operations were part of efforts to curb undocumented migration and prosecute employers who engage or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. “These ongoing enforcement operations reflect the authorities’ steadfast commitment to curbing the presence of undocumented migrants and taking firm action against any employers who harbor or employ them,” he said. However, the report did not disclose the identities of the Nigerians arrested or the specific locations where the arrests were made. item.title: 2027: Wike Criticises Obi Over National Anthem Snub At NDC Lagos Town Hall Meeting
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, demonstrated lawlessness and an intent to divide Nigeria by allegedly refusing to recite the official one. Wike made these remarks on Friday, during a stakeholders’ town hall meeting in Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State, organised under the banner of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates. ﻿ Addressing traditional rulers, community leaders, youths, and party faithful, the FCT minister argued that a leader who disregards national symbols cannot be trusted with the presidency. “A whole national anthem of a country is being sung. A man who wants to be President of Nigeria would disobey and sit down. And then not only that, when a different national anthem that is not being used for Nigeria [was sung], he stood up. “In a way, he does not belong to this country. In a way, he has said he does not belong to this country; that if you give him the president, he would do a different thing that will divide Nigeria. “A man who does not believe in Nigeria, someone who derives joy in ridiculing the country by disrespecting its symbolic National Anthem must not be allowed to come near the presidency of our country,” the minister said. Wike further criticised Obi’s political trajectory and past governance record, alleging that the former Anambra State governor frequently abandons political parties whenever internal crises arise, rather than staying to resolve them. He also faulted Obi for not conducting local government elections during his eight-year tenure as governor, describing it as a contradiction to his professed belief in the rule of law. Tackles Atiku, Amaechi In addition to targeting Obi, the FCT Minister took aim at the opposition coalition involving former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi. Wike questioned their track records in public office, specifically citing the state of seaports during Amaechi’s tenure as Minister of Transportation and alleging that the administration demolished Government Secondary School, Ogu, without rebuilding it, alongside unfulfilled promises regarding a 1,000-bed specialist hospital. Urging the people of Ogu-Bolo to disregard what he termed “big grammar” from opposition politicians on television, Wike maintained that President Bola Tinubu’s administration had delivered tangible dividends of democracy to the area. He pointed to the construction of the Ogu-Bolo Civic Centre—facilitated through the federal appointment of an indigene, Boma Iyaye—as well as the conduct of local government elections. He urged people in the area to massively support the re-election of Tinubu, Kingsley Chinda for Governor of Rivers State and all the APC candidates seeking National Assembly seats. item.title: It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction
item.description: As of this morning, Microsoft is still scrambling to restore service following yesterday's global outage, with millions of users unable to access Outlook and other vital tools. It's not the end of the world, but it does seem fitting that this should happen on the day a physicist predicted would be the end of humanity: November 13, 2026. And it falls on a Friday, too. The physicist in question is Heinz von Foerster, who published a 1960 paper in the journal Science predicting that by today, overpopulation would reach the breaking point. It's not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus —one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever. Population dynamics are notoriously tricky to calculate because there are so many variables to consider and so much unpredictability in the system. In his 1960 analysis, Von Foerster accurately measured past trends in population growth, but like Malthus, he assumed those trends would carry into the future largely unchanged. So he projected that human population growth would march inexorably toward infinity. We wouldn't starve to death; von Foerster thought we would be ingenious enough to solve the food supply problem. Instead, "they will be squeezed to death," he wrote. Read full article Comments

item.title: Over 300 Pro-Crypto Lawmakers Are Coming Into Congress
item.description: ▶ Bitcoin Magazine Over 300 Pro-Crypto Lawmakers Are Coming Into Congress Mason Lynaugh, executive director of Stand With Crypto, joins BMTV to talk through what the midterms mean for Bitcoin and crypto. Stand With Crypto’s race tracker showed 29 of 45 endorsed candidates winning. Mason’s first reason for optimism is the makeup of Congress itself: about 96 pro-crypto members in 2023, and over 300 heading into the 120th, which he calls a pro-crypto majority you could get excited about. The second is that crypto voters made their voices heard in tight races. In Darren Soto’s Florida 9, Soto won by around 1,400 votes in a district with 11,000 Stand With Crypto advocates, and Mason says they genuinely think crypto voters moved that election. item.title: I saw Saturn’s rings in seconds with the Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian telescope — full review
item.description: null Saturn was only a night past its annual opposition when I pointed the Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian straight at it. The planet was at its biggest and brightest of the year, the seeing was good and its famous rings were visibly opening up after appearing edge-on from Earth in recent years. It was an obvious target for a new telescope. Finding it took seconds. After selecting Saturn in Celestron’s StarSense Explorer app, I followed the on-screen arrows as I moved the telescope across the sky. As I got closer, the app zoomed in until a bullseye turned green. I looked through the supplied 25mm eyepiece, then swapped to the 10mm to see a pale yellow Saturn at 75x magnification, with its rings sharply defined and its giant moon Titan visible in orbit. At 25 lbs (11.33 kg), the Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian is a relative heavyweight. Jamie Carter The supplied 25mm and 10mm Kellner eyepieces provide 30x and 75x magnification, respectively, but are obvious candidates for future upgrades. Jamie Carter The StarSense Explorer smartphone dock uses a small mirror. Jamie Carter It was a stunning view, and exactly the kind of experience a beginner needs from a first telescope. There was no frustration and no wondering whether I was looking in the right place. StarSense took me straight there — but, crucially, I moved the telescope myself. I’ve always liked that combination of hand-holding and DIY observing that Celestron’s StarSense tech gives you. I’m less convinced by the tabletop telescope it’s attached to. Although this $599 RRP (£379) model is significantly smaller than the Celestron StarSense Explorer 8-inch Dobsonian telescope I’ve previously reviewed, it still weighs 25 lbs (11.33 kg). You need to place it on something sturdy before you can use it comfortably. After living with it in my backyard, I’m not convinced the tabletop format is the advantage it initially appears to be. An iPhone 16 Pro Max fitted securely into the StarSense Explorer smartphone dock during testing. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) What StarSense Explorer does well The Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian comes with a red dot finder for manual navigation. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I’ve used Celestron’s StarSense Explorer system on a variety of telescopes and have always been impressed by how easy this type of smartphone navigation is to use. The technology works just as well here and, for me, it remains one of the best ways of making a traditional optical telescope accessible to a complete beginner. This isn’t a computerized GoTo telescope. There are no motors to slew across the sky automatically and no tracking system to keep an object centered. Instead, a smartphone sits in a dock attached to the telescope, and its camera looks at the sky via a small mirror. Celestron’s StarSense Explorer app analyzes the reflections of the stars it sees, works out exactly where the telescope is pointing and tells you which dir

item.title: Astronaut Suni Williams rides through NYC as Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade | Space photo of the day for Nov. 13, 2026
item.description: null NASA astronaut Suni Williams rides through New York City as the Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: Photo by Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images) New Yorkers got a space-y surprise on Wednesday (Nov. 11): Retired NASA astronaut and U.S. Navy Captain Sunita "Suni" Williams rolled down 5th Avenue in the back of a classic convertible wrapped in patriotic decals as Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade. What is it? On Wednesday, New York City's 107th annual Veterans Day Parade made its way through Manhattan to the cheers and respectful nods of thousands of onlookers. The parade is an annual tradition on the holiday, which honors veterans of the U.S. armed forces. As part of the parade, veterans, active-duty soldiers, firefighters, marching bands, youth cadets and more march through the city and honor those who have served and sacrificed in the U.S. military. This year, the parade featured Suni Williams as its grand marshal. "I’m proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honoring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation," she said during the event. Why is it incredible? Williams was selected for NASA's astronaut program in 1998 and retired from it in December 2025 . She spent 608 days in space during her astronaut career, the second-most by an American astronaut behind Peggy Whitson , who racked up 695. Williams also had an extensive career in the U.S. Navy. She began as an ensign in 1987 before serving in a number of different roles. For example, she was a diving officer and a naval aviator and also provided helicopter combat support during Operation Desert Shield and Operation Provide Comfort. She further served as a squadron safety officer and finally as a captain, a rank she achieved in 2017. During this time, Williams supported relief efforts following Hurricane Andrew, trained within the U.S. Naval Test Pilot School and gained a wealth of further experience flying as a military pilot. Williams is part of a longstanding tradition of astronauts serving in the U.S. military. From test pilots to naval officers and more, there's a strong link between the U.S. armed forces and NASA's astronaut program.

item.title: FG Signs Port Harcourt Airport Concession Agreement, Assures Workers’ Protection
item.description: The Federal Government has signed a concession agreement for the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt, with PH Airport Limited, following assurances from the concessionaire that the arrangement would not lead to job losses. The agreement was signed at the office of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, in Abuja, on Thursday. The Federal Government delegation was led by Keyamo, while PH Airport Limited was represented by its Group Managing Director, Eyo Asuquo. The signing followed a meeting between the minister and aviation union leaders to discuss the implications of the concession for airport workers. Speaking on behalf of the unions, Comrade Ben Nnabue said organised labour had approved the agreement after receiving assurances that no aviation worker would lose their job as a result of the arrangement. He said job security remained a major concern for the unions and that they were satisfied with the commitments made before endorsing the agreement. Photo of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and the federal government delegation in Abuja, on Thursday. Also speaking, Asuquo highlighted Port Harcourt’s strategic importance in the Gulf of Guinea, describing the airport as a potential gateway for regional commerce, investment and connectivity. He said PH Airport Limited intended to improve the airport’s infrastructure and operational standards, adding that the concession would create more employment opportunities rather than result in job losses. According to him, the company’s vision extends beyond managing the facility to expanding airport-related activities, attracting investment and unlocking its economic potential. The Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, Chris Najomo; Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; ministry directors and aviation union leaders attended the event. The concession agreement was subsequently signed by the concessionaire and relevant ministry officials, with Keyamo presiding over the ceremony. The Federal Government said the agreement was part of its broader efforts to attract private-sector investment and expertise into the development and management of Nigeria’s airport infrastructure. Under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development has pursued reforms aimed at modernising airports, improving operational efficiency and strengthening the aviation sector’s contribution to economic growth. The Port Harcourt airport concession is expected to improve the passenger experience, strengthen airport services, and attract investment to the facility. item.title: Screenless GPS: Slate Auto says, "Remember the road atlas"
item.description: Whether it's nostalgia or a sense that technology has gotten a bit too pervasive, there’s no denying that Slate Auto appears to be tuned into the particular moment. The startup has a simple pitch : an affordable electric truck with just the basics , leaving owners to DIY and BYOD for everything else, all for a sub-$25,000 starting price. Among the things Slate does without is an embedded infotainment system. The small digital display on the dashboard that shows your speed and range is also where the backup camera appears if you engage reverse, and there are two USB-C ports that provide power but not connectivity, and that’s that. But there is a solution to getting lost, and it's called “Screenless GPS.” Even though we don’t have a Slate truck to test it with, the OEM sent us a unit to review. That’s right, it’s a good old spiral-bound road atlas! “We believe you should use the devices you know and love,” Slate says, and it reckons that maps worked just fine for past generations, so they should still work now. item.title: President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them. Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported. Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber. Who the nominees are Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules. Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance. Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner. Lame-duck timing and a Democratic Senate The timing puts the nominees in front of a Senate in its lame-duck session, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s sharpest critics, is expected to chair the Banking Committee when the new Congress is seated in January. The pairing of Democrats with Republicans could matter for confirmation. After the election, TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg told clients he did not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees

item.title: Most affairs don't matter except to the people involved. Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen's blunder will rock the world
item.description: It's a story as old as time. Billionaire nerd boy meets girl. Girl is later suspected of being a spy. News at 11. Oh, and it's also been reported that he was having an affair with one of his direct-report employees. When Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang makes a "romantic" blunder, he doesn't do it halfway. The boss of the world's most valuable company – well, it was until recently, anyway – publicly resigned yesterday, November 12, as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately. We don't know if he jumped or if he was pushed. He left after admitting to having an affair. Although he never named an affair partner, one of the affairs was reported to be with Alice Huang, AKA Huang Le. She's head of the Chinese company Megaspeed, which was an Nvidia partner. Megaspeed is accused of being a front for China's government that was used to transfer Nvidia chips to China, although this hasn't been proven. Some US officials also suspect [PDF] she's working for Chinese intelligence, although the DoJ said it hasn't yet reached a conclusion about this. The final nail in Jensen's coffin came when The New York Times reported he had also allegedly had an affair with Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. Jeeze, guy! In the aftermath, Nvidia's CFO, Colette Kress, was appointed interim CEO. She won't, I suspect, be in the job for long. CFOs are not CEOs. The jobs aren't remotely the same. In most companies, Huang would be replaced by the COO. That can't happen here. Nvidia doesn't have a COO. Both inside and outside of Nvidia, Huang is seen as Nvidia, and Nvidia as Huang. These days, billionaire CEOs are perceived as God-kings who know all and rule all. Much more often than not, that's BS. That isn't the case with Nvidia. Huang co-founded Nvidia on April 5, 1993. He was appointed CEO on day one, and he never left the job. At first, the company staggered forward. When it released the GeForce 256 in 1999 , which it marketed as the first GPU, it started on its path to becoming the chip manufacturer of choice for PC gamers. It still is today. That's a great niche, but it doesn't make a company a trillion-dollar business. No, the path to that dizzying height came when, in 2006, Nvidia unveiled CUDA . This programming architecture opened its GPUs' parallel-processing capabilities to scientific and other non-graphics workloads. From there, CUDA would become the foundation for most high-performance and AI computing. Huang was at the center of it all. He still was until now. At KubeCon North America , the trade show for Kubernetes, used in well over half of all AI projects, I spoke to many Nvidia employees. There were two things they all mentioned. First, they were in a state of shock. Maybe the top brass and government officials both in China and the US knew Huang was fooling with fire; the developer rank-and-file folks I spoke to hadn't had a clue. item.title: Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029
item.description: ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming. Climate Action Tracker , a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5° Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicus climate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement . When the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7° Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus. Read full article Comments
